events.title: US-Israel war on Iran and the Gulf energy shock

tags.why: As of 31 Oct 2026 Tehran is still setting conditions for reopening Hormuz, while Washington says the strait is secure. Trump is weighing new strikes after the 3 Nov midterms, with a 4 Nov date reported, and Iran threatens a wider war in response, so transits face delays, war-risk
tags.action: Ask your forwarder for current war-risk surcharges and Gulf-bound routing options. Add 10 days of buffer stock for Gulf-origin or Gulf-bound cargo, and ask about overland or alternative-port options.

tags.why: Jebel Ali lies inside the Gulf behind Hormuz, so the strait restrictions and the risk of renewed US-Iran strikes around 4 Nov mean longer waits and added surcharges for cargo calling there.
tags.action: Ask your carrier whether Jebel Ali calls are being skipped or transshipped. Pre-book alternatives such as Red Sea or Omani ports for time-critical boxes, and add about a week of buffer.

tags.why: Trump's camp has threatened attacks from 4 Nov and Iran's supreme leader has ordered an immediate response to any threat, so air cargo routings over Iran are likely to be closed or avoided, lengthening Europe-Asia flights.
tags.action: Ask your air forwarder to confirm routings that avoid Iranian airspace and to quote the added transit time and fuel surcharge. Move urgent shipments off Gulf-corridor flights before 4 Nov.

tags.why: Iran threatens wider strikes if the US or Israel attacks again after the midterms, so Israeli, Lebanese and Jordanian airspace could close on short notice and force air freight to divert.
tags.action: Ask your air forwarder for a fallback routing that avoids the Levant, and avoid single-routing time-critical air freight through the region in the first week of November.

tags.why: Renewed fighting in Yemen and the risk of the Iran war restarting after the midterms raise the chance of attacks on shipping at Bab el-Mandeb in the next 30 days.
tags.action: Ask your forwarder whether Asia-Europe bookings are being routed via the Cape of Good Hope. Allow 14 extra days of transit and confirm who pays war-risk surcharges.

events.title: OPEC+ freezes quotas as Gulf exports run at 60-80% of normal

tags.why: On 2026-10-30 the IRGC reported three tankers on fire after hitting mines on the IMO-approved Hormuz route, and Gulf exports are already running at only 60-80% of normal, so transits face delays, convoy waits and war-risk premiums.
tags.action: Ask your forwarder for the current war-risk surcharge and the vessel's Hormuz routing, hold a 10-day buffer on Gulf-origin cargo, and get quotes for alternatives such as Red Sea ports with a land bridge.

tags.why: Jebel Ali lies inside the Gulf behind Hormuz, and the mine strikes on tankers reported 2026-10-30 add to restricted and irregular transits, so vessel calls to and from the port face schedule slippage and extra surcharges.
tags.action: Confirm sailing schedules and any Gulf emergency surcharges with your carrier before booking, and build 7 days of buffer stock for cargo shipped via Jebel Ali.

events.title: Spain's November strike and snap election

tags.why: A Spanish general strike is reported for 11 November 2026, and coverage warns of wider transport delays, so dockworkers, truckers and customs staff at Valencia could join and slow gate and vessel handling for a day or two.
tags.action: Ask your forwarder to move container pick-ups and deliveries at Valencia off 10-12 November, and add 2 days of buffer stock for cargo due that week.

tags.why: Roads in Istanbul were closed by flooding after the 15 October rains, and forecasts from 31 October show a week of heavy rain from the start of November, so truck access to the Ambarlı terminals may be slowed.
tags.action: Ask your forwarder or trucker for Ambarlı gate-in and pickup times for the first two weeks of November, and add 2 days of buffer to container cut-offs for Istanbul-area suppliers.
